The answer names three macros (C, PTHREAD, ALT) and never says which two the item means. It also says it could not confirm the shipped default from the index. || QUOTE: `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` defaults to off (`include/mbedtls/mbedtls_config.h:3787`). `MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD` and `MBEDTLS_THREADING_ALT` also default to off. | WHY: The answer says the threading macros default to off, but it never says the shipped mbedtls_config.h leaves them undefined, so a default build defines neither. It also names a different pair of macros (THREADING_PTHREAD and THREADING_ALT alongside THREADING_C), and it says it could not confirm the shipped default from the index. || QUOTE: `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` defaults to off (`include/mbedtls/mbedtls_config.h:3787`). `MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD` and `MBEDTLS_THREADING_ALT` also default to off. | WHY: The answer says the threading macros default to off, but it does not say they are left undefined in the shipped config, and it names THREADING_ALT where the item means the two macros THREADING_C and THREADING_PTHREAD. decisions.mark: states BOTH halves of the contrast: that nothing in library/ creates a thread, AND that library/ nonetheless supplies the mutex abstraction used by threaded callers

The contrast is not stated as the item requires. || QUOTE: NONE | WHY: The answer says the library creates no threads, but it describes the mutex code in library/threading.c only as protecting library state.
